title: Discover your local institutions
summary: Learn how the town council works, who belongs to it and which public services care for your municipality.
keyIdeas: The town council governs and organises a municipality.
The municipal government includes the mayor and councillors.
Local voters elect councillors every four years in municipal elections.

basicKnowledge: C. Sociedades y territorios › Alfabetización cívica

activities.prompt: In which building does a municipality's government work? 🏛️
activities.explanation: The town hall is the building where the government team works and manages municipal affairs.

activities.prompt: The mayor makes every decision alone, without anyone's help.
activities.explanation: The mayor works as a team with councillors to govern the municipality.

activities.prompt: Match each municipal service to its main job.
activities.explanation: The council organises public services to keep the municipality clean, safe and cared for.

pairs.right: Managing traffic and looking after safety
Sweeping streets and emptying rubbish bins
Caring for trees and green spaces
Lending books and organising reading workshops

activities.prompt: Complete the sentence about local elections.
activities.explanation: In Spain, ordinary municipal elections take place every four years to renew local government.
activities.hint: Think about the usual length of a municipal term of office.
activities.sentence: In ordinary municipal elections, councillors are elected every ___ years.

activities.prompt: Sort these tasks by who is responsible for them.
activities.explanation: The council looks after public spaces, while families take care of household tasks.

items.text: Clearing and washing the dinner dishes

activities.prompt: Read the school news story and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: The council chamber is where representatives debate public decisions. Taxes help pay for local improvements.
activities.title: Primary Grade 3 visits the council chamber
activities.text: Today, the Primary Grade 3 class visited their town hall. The mayor, Nuria, welcomed them into the council chamber. She explained that councillors meet there to debate and vote on local improvements. The pupils asked about the new playground and the cycle lane to school. Nuria explained that the municipal budget pays for these projects using taxes paid by residents. Finally, the children sat in the councillors' seats and held a pretend vote to choose a tree for their playground.

questions.prompt: Where are council decisions debated and voted on?
questions.explanation: Councillors meet in the council chamber to debate and vote.

questions.prompt: How are municipal services and building projects paid for?
questions.explanation: The mayor explains that residents' taxes help fund these projects.

activities.prompt: Put these steps in a municipality's democratic process in order.
activities.explanation: First, parties present their ideas. Voters then elect councillors, who choose the mayor.
items: Parties explain their proposals to residents
Voters cast their votes in ballot boxes
Councillors from the parties are elected

activities.prompt: Omar and Lucía see a broken swing in their neighbourhood park. What should their families do? 🛝
activities.explanation: The council is responsible for maintaining and repairing municipal playgrounds.
activities.hint: Think about which institution manages public play areas.
options: Report it to the council through its residents' service
Call the hospital to request an ambulance
Wait for rain to see whether it fixes itself

activities.prompt: Registered local residents can attend public council meetings as audience members.
activities.explanation: Municipal council meetings are public so people can learn how decisions about their town or city are made.

activities.prompt: Aisha's village wants a safe cycle lane to the school. Who should debate and approve this public project? 🚲
activities.explanation: The council decides on improvements to municipal streets. Full council meetings approve matters such as budgets; specific responsibilities are shared among its governing bodies.
options: The mayor and councillors at a full council meeting
The headteacher and school meal supervisors
